description: Remove reentrancy patches, collapse handler error handling to the durable dispatcher, and clean up the epic reconcile misnomer + poll-driven sweep after #362's durable delivery landed.

tasks.title: Restore turn-based serialization on authority grains and add concurrency specs
tasks.spec: specs/grain-turn-serialization/spec.md#Authority grains rely solely on Orleans turn-based serialization
tasks.description: Remove [Reentrant] from WorkflowGrain (WorkflowGrain.cs:22) and RunnerGrain (RunnerGrain.cs:33); remove RunnerGrain._worksStateWriteGate (RunnerGrain.cs:43) and simplify PersistAsync to call _worksState.WriteStateAsync() directly. Clean up stale [Reentrant] prose in WorkflowStageLockReleaseHandler.cs:21-23. Add two concurrency characteristic spec files (WorkflowGrainConcurrencySpecs, RunnerGrainConcurrencySpecs) mirroring the existing WorkflowGrainFixture pattern: InProcessTestCluster + MigratedSqliteTemplate + FakeTimeProvider, asserting final settled state consistency under multiple control/work-mutating operations without reentrancy.
acceptanceCriteria: WorkflowGrain does not carry the [Reentrant] attribute and its `using Orleans.Concurrency` is dropped if no symbol from that namespace remains
RunnerGrain does not carry the [Reentrant] attribute and its `using Orleans.Concurrency` is dropped if no symbol from that namespace remains
RunnerGrain._worksStateWriteGate SemaphoreSlim field is removed; PersistAsync calls _worksState.WriteStateAsync() directly without gate acquisition/release
All 11 PersistAsync call sites (RunnerGrain.cs lines 116,145,167,194,273,341,355,382,484,645,706) compile and behave unchanged
WorkflowStageLockReleaseHandler.cs XML doc no longer references [Reentrant] or in-stack delivery; prose describes the awaited dispatch model

WorkflowGrainConcurrencySpecs exists under packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.SpecTests/Specs/Workflow/ and issues multiple control operations (start/pause/resume/retry/rerun) against one activation, asserting in-memory run state and persisted snapshot remain internally consistent

RunnerGrainConcurrencySpecs exists under packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.SpecTests/Specs/Runner/Grain/ and issues multiple work-mutating operations (assign work, report result, closeout on presence loss) against one activation without reentrancy and without a write gate, asserting works ledger and persisted state remain internally consistent
Both concurrency spec files use InProcessTestCluster + MigratedSqliteTemplate.CopyTo + FakeTimeProvider; no real clustering, no real DB, no wall-clock waits, no order dependencies
Concurrency specs assert only on final settled state, never on interleaving timing
npm run build succeeds (TreatWarningsAsErrors catches any missed reference)
npm test passes (server specs, including the two new concurrency spec files)
tasks.output: Modified WorkflowGrain.cs, RunnerGrain.cs, WorkflowStageLockReleaseHandler.cs; new WorkflowGrainConcurrencySpecs.cs and RunnerGrainConcurrencySpecs.cs spec files
tasks.notes: Re-run the self-reentrancy audit at implementation time: verify no await path in either grain resolves a call back into the SAME grain activation via IGrainFactory/GrainFactory.GetGrain<SelfGrainType>. Verified absent today; the new concurrency specs are the running safety net.

tasks.title: Collapse handler error handling to the durable dispatcher
tasks.spec: specs/handler-error-propagation/spec.md#Event handlers propagate failures to the durable dispatcher
tasks.description: Remove the catch-log-return wrapper in AgentSubscriptionDispatchHandler.HandleAsync (lines 79-92) so subscription dispatch failures propagate to the durable dispatcher; keep envelope-level no-op returns and OperationCanceledException rethrow. Remove the outer setup try-catch in HermesIssueNotificationHandler.HandleAsync (lines 50-74) so setup failures propagate; keep the background DeliverAsync try-catch (best-effort UI push channel) and the disabled-notification/unconfigured-webhook early returns. Verify RunnerWorkflowTerminalStatusHandler awaits the router synchronously and has no stale detach/in-stack prose.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentSubscriptionDispatchHandler.HandleAsync no longer wraps its dispatch body in a try-catch that logs-and-returns on non-cancellation exceptions (the catch (Exception ex) block at lines 87-92 is removed)
AgentSubscriptionDispatchHandler.HandleAsync still rethrows OperationCanceledException when ct.IsCancellationRequested
AgentSubscriptionDispatchHandler.HandleAsync still returns a completed task for envelope-level no-ops (no projectid, no active matched subscription, empty rendered prompt) without throwing
HermesIssueNotificationHandler.HandleAsync no longer wraps its setup body in a try-catch that logs-and-returns on non-cancellation exceptions (the outer try-catch at lines 50-74 is removed)
HermesIssueNotificationHandler.HandleAsync still returns a completed task for disabled notification types and unconfigured webhooks without throwing

HermesIssueNotificationHandler.DeliverAsync retains its own try-catch (lines 79-101) and BackgroundHermesIssueNotificationDispatcher retains its Task.Run catch — the best-effort channel's own error handling is preserved
RunnerWorkflowTerminalStatusHandler.HandleAsync awaits IRunnerWorkflowStatusRouter.RouteAsync synchronously on the dispatch stack; no detach/fire-and-forget
RunnerWorkflowTerminalStatusHandler XML doc and prose describe the awaited-delivery model; no references to detach, in-stack delivery, or synchronous-callback deadlock workarounds remain

Handler tests updated to verify that non-cancellation exceptions thrown during HandleAsync propagate to the dispatcher (retry/DLQ path), and that envelope-level no-op outcomes still return without throwing
npm run build succeeds (TreatWarningsAsErrors)
npm test passes (server specs)
tasks.output: Modified AgentSubscriptionDispatchHandler.cs, HermesIssueNotificationHandler.cs, RunnerWorkflowTerminalStatusHandler.cs; updated handler test files
tasks.notes: Do NOT remove the DeliverAsync try-catch in HermesIssueNotificationHandler — it is the best-effort UI-push channel's own error handling (design/architecture.md two-channel split), not a dispatcher-level swallow. Only the setup-phase try-catch propagates.

tasks.title: Remove the poll-driven epic sweep and rename reconcile to recompute progress

Then rename the full epic progress-recompute chain: IEpicGrain.ReconcileAfterTerminalAsync -> RecomputeProgressAsync, EpicGrain.ReconcileAfterTerminalInternalAsync -> RecomputeProgressInternalAsync (including the ResumeAsync:524 call site), EpicReconcileDispatcher -> EpicProgressRecomputeDispatcher, EpicCancelledReconcileHandler -> EpicCancelledHandler. Update all XML doc, <see cref>, and test method names referencing the old reconcile naming across EpicProgressionSpecs.cs, EpicAutoDoneSpecs.cs, and EpicAutoDoneHandlerSpecs.cs. Behavior is unchanged.
